title: Alert rule DB column types must match the int64 model fields, in both alert_rule and alert_rule_version
answers: saving alert rule with large missing series evaluations to resolve fails
missing_series_evals_to_resolve out of range smallint error on MySQL/Postgres
why does alert_rule_version need the same migration as alert_rule
how to widen an alert rule column type
body:
Symptom: an alert rule with "missing series evaluations to resolve" set above 32,767 fails to save (out of range) on MySQL or PostgreSQL.
Root cause: the column was added as SMALLINT by pkg/services/sqlstore/migrations/ualert/alert_rule_missing_series_evals_to_resolve.go:AddAlertRuleMissingSeriesEvalsToResolve, but the model field MissingSeriesEvalsToResolve is *int64.
Fix pattern: leave the original migration as is. Add a new migration (ExpandAlertRuleMissingSeriesEvalsToResolve) that widens the column to nullable BIGINT. Add a regression test in pkg/services/ngalert/store/alert_rule_test.go:TestIntegrationUpdateAlertRules that stores a value above the limit and reads it back from both the rule (GetAlertRuleByUID) and the alertRuleVersion row.
Constraints: every rule column exists in both alert_rule and alert_rule_version, so a type change needs one migration per table. Otherwise version history writes still overflow. Only MySQL and Postgres SQL was added. SQLite was not altered.
applies: Schema changes to ngalert alert_rule / alert_rule_version columns
